summary: Small amounts of different holy things can be added together to make the full amount for me'ilah, and for the issurim of piggul, nosar and tamei.

chunks.he: קָדְשֵׁי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה לִמְעִילָה,
chunks.en: Holy things of the mizbeach join together for me'ilah,
chunks.st: All items consecrated to be sacrificed on the altar join together to constitute the measure with regard to liability for misuse
chunks.stMore: of consecrated property, which is deriving benefit equivalent to one peruta.

words.note: Small amounts are added up to make the full amount.
Me'ilah is using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for yourself.

chunks.en: and to make one punished because of piggul,
chunks.st: And they join together to constitute an olive-bulk, which is the measure that renders one liable due to violation of the prohibitions of piggul,

words.note: A korban made pasul by a wrong thought about when it would be eaten.

chunks.en: nosar, or tamei.
chunks.st: or notar, or partaking of the item while ritually impure.

words.note: Meat of a korban left over past its time.

chunks.he: קָדְשֵׁי בֶדֶק הַבַּיִת מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
chunks.en: Holy things for fixing the Beis HaMikdash join together.
chunks.st: All items consecrated for Temple maintenance join together
chunks.stMore: to constitute the measure with regard to liability for misuse.

words.note: Bedek HaBayis: things given for fixing and building the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: Holy things of the mizbeach and holy things for fixing the Beis HaMikdash
chunks.st: Both items consecrated to be sacrificed on the altar and items consecrated for Temple maintenance

chunks.en: join together for me'ilah.
chunks.st: join together to constitute the measure with regard to liability for misuse.

summary: The parts of an olah and its mincha and wine join together, and so do the parts of a todah. Terumah, challah and bikkurim also join together.

chunks.he: חֲמִשָּׁה דְבָרִים בָּעוֹלָה מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
chunks.en: Five things in an olah join together.
chunks.st: Five items in the burnt offering and the accompanying meal offering and libation join together
chunks.stMore: to constitute the one peruta measure with regard to liability for misuse, and the olive-bulk measure with regard to liability for piggul, notar, and partaking of sacrificial foods while ritually impure.

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbeach.

chunks.en: The meat, and the fats,
chunks.st: They are: The flesh; the fat
chunks.stMore: of the burnt offering that is sacrificed on the altar;

chunks.en: and the flour, and the wine,
chunks.st: the fine flour of the accompanying meal offering; the wine
chunks.stMore: of the accompanying libation;

chunks.en: and the oil. And six in a todah:
chunks.st: and the oil of the accompanying meal offering. And there are six items in the thanks offering
chunks.stMore: that join together:

words.note: A korban brought to thank Hashem.

chunks.en: The meat, and the fats,
chunks.st: The flesh, the fat,

chunks.en: and the flour, and the wine,
chunks.st: the fine flour, the wine,

chunks.en: and the oil, and the bread.
chunks.st: the oil, and the loaves
chunks.stMore: accompanying the thanks offering.

chunks.en: Terumah, and terumas maaser,
chunks.st: Teruma, and teruma of the tithe,

words.note: A gift of food given to the Kohanim.

chunks.en: and terumas maaser of demai,
chunks.st: and teruma of the tithe of doubtfully tithed produce [demai],

words.note: Food bought from someone who may not have taken off maaser.

chunks.en: challah, and bikkurim,
chunks.st: and ḥalla, and first fruits

words.note: A piece of dough given to the Kohen.
The first fruits brought to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: join together to make a mixture forbidden,
chunks.st: all join together with one another to constitute the requisite measure to prohibit a mixture with non-sacred produce,

chunks.en: and to make one pay the extra fifth for them.
chunks.st: and to form the requisite measure of an olive-bulk that serves to render one obligated for their consumption in payment of an additional one-fifth over and above the principal.

words.note: When one pays back, he adds one fifth more.

summary: Pieces of the same kind of issur or tumah join together. Rabbi Yehoshua's rule: things join only if their tumah and their amount are the same.

chunks.he: כָּל הַפִּגּוּלִין מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
chunks.en: All piggul pieces join together.
chunks.st: All the pieces of sacrificial meat that are piggul join together with one another to constitute the olive-bulk measure for liability,

chunks.he: כָּל הַנּוֹתָרִין מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
chunks.en: All nosar pieces join together.
chunks.st: and all sacrificial meat that is notar joins together with one another to constitute the olive-bulk measure for liability.

chunks.he: כָּל הַנְּבֵלוֹת מִצְטָרְפוֹת זוֹ עִם זוֹ.
chunks.en: All neveilos join together.
chunks.st: All animal carcasses, whose consumption is prohibited and which transmit impurity through contact with them and through carrying, join together with one another to constitute the requisite olive-bulk measure.

words.note: Animals that died without shechitah.

chunks.he: כָּל הַשְּׁרָצִים מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
chunks.en: All sheratzim join together.
chunks.st: And all repugnant creatures join together with one another to constitute the requisite olive-bulk measure to render one who consumes it liable to receive lashes.
chunks.stMore: The eight creeping animals enumerated in the Torah join together to constitute the measure of a lentil-bulk, which transmits impurity through contact, and to render one who consumes it liable to receive lashes.

words.note: Small creeping animals, like mice, that are not kosher.

chunks.en: The blood of a sheretz and its meat join together.
chunks.st: The blood of one of the eight creeping animals listed in the Torah and their flesh join together to constitute the lentil-bulk measure to impart impurity.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said a rule:
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua stated a principle:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: Anything whose tumah and amount are the same,
chunks.st: With regard to any items whose impurity, in terms of degree and duration, and measure to impart impurity, are equal,
chunks.stMore: e.g., two halves of an olive-bulk from two corpses or two animal carcasses or two halves of a lentil-bulk from two creeping animals,

chunks.en: they join together.
chunks.st: they join together to constitute the requisite measure.

chunks.en: If the tumah is the same but not the amount,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua continued: By contrast, with regard to items whose impurity is equal but their measure is not equal,
chunks.stMore: e.g., a creeping animal and an animal carcass, each of which renders one impure until the evening, but the measure of a creeping animal is a lentil-bulk, whereas that of an animal carcass is an olive-bulk;

chunks.en: the amount but not the tumah,
chunks.st: or items whose measure is equal but whose impurity is not equal,
chunks.stMore: e.g., a corpse and an animal carcass, with regard to which the measure of each is an olive-bulk, but the duration of the impurity imparted by a corpse is one week and the duration of the impurity imparted by an animal carcass is until the evening;

chunks.en: not the tumah and not the amount,
chunks.st: or items that are equal neither in terms of their impurity nor in terms of their measure,

chunks.en: they do not join together.
chunks.st: they do not join together to constitute the requisite measure.

summary: Piggul and nosar do not join together, and neither do different kinds of tumah. But food that became tamei from a stronger or weaker source of tumah does join together.

chunks.he: הַפִּגּוּל וְהַנּוֹתָר אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה,
chunks.en: Piggul and nosar do not join together,
chunks.st: Sacrificial meat that is piggul and sacrificial meat that is notar do not join together
chunks.stMore: to constitute the requisite measure of an olive-bulk,

chunks.en: because they are two different names.
chunks.st: due to the fact that they belong to two separate categories of prohibition.

chunks.en: A sheretz and a neveilah,
chunks.st: The flesh of the carcass of the creeping animal and the flesh of the animal carcass,

chunks.en: and so too a neveilah and the flesh of a dead person,
chunks.st: and likewise the flesh of the animal carcass and the flesh of the corpse,

chunks.en: do not join together
chunks.st: do not join together

chunks.en: to make tamei, not even like the lighter of the two.
chunks.st: to transmit ritual impurity, not even for the more lenient of the two impurities,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the impurity that requires the greater measure.

chunks.en: Food that became tamei from an av hatumah
chunks.st: The food that became ritually impure through contact with a primary source of ritual impurity,
chunks.stMore: thereby assuming first-degree ritual impurity,

words.note: An av hatumah is a main source of tumah.

chunks.en: and food that became tamei from a vlad hatumah,
chunks.st: and the food that became ritually impure through contact with a secondary source of ritual impurity,
chunks.stMore: thereby assuming second-degree ritual impurity,

words.note: Something that became tamei from a main source.

chunks.en: join together
chunks.st: join together
chunks.stMore: to constitute the requisite measure of an egg-bulk

chunks.en: to make tamei like the lighter of the two.
chunks.st: to transmit impurity in accordance with the more lenient of the two, i.e., second-degree ritual impurity.

summary: All kinds of food join together to make the amounts used in many halachos: for eating tamei food, for an eruv, for tumah of food, for carrying on Shabbos and for eating on Yom Kippur. Drinks also join together.

chunks.en: All foods join together
chunks.st: All the ritually impure foods join together

chunks.en: to make the body pasul, with half of a peras,
chunks.explain: Eating that much tamei food stops one from eating terumah.
chunks.st: to constitute the requisite measure to disqualify the body [hageviyya] of one who eats half of a half-loaf-bulk [peras] of the impure foods from partaking of teruma.

words.note: A half-loaf amount.

chunks.en: with food for two meals for the eruv,
chunks.st: Likewise, all foods join together to constitute the requisite measure of food sufficient for two meals, to establish a joining of Shabbat boundaries;

words.note: An eruv techumin lets a person walk farther on Shabbos.

chunks.en: with an egg's size to make tamei with the tumah of food,
chunks.st: and to form the requisite measure of an egg-bulk, to render an item impure with the ritual impurity of food;

chunks.en: with a dried fig's size for carrying out on Shabbos,
chunks.st: and to form the measure of a dried fig-bulk, which establishes liability for carrying out food on Shabbat;

chunks.en: with a big date's size on Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: and to form the volume of a large date, which establishes liability for eating on Yom Kippur.

chunks.en: All drinks join together
chunks.st: All the liquids join together

chunks.en: to make the body pasul, with a revi'is,
chunks.st: to constitute the requisite measure to disqualify the body of one who drinks a quarter-log of ritually impure liquid from partaking of teruma;

words.note: A small cupful.

chunks.en: and with a cheekful on Yom Kippur.
chunks.st: and to constitute the measure of a cheekful, which establishes liability for drinking on Yom Kippur.

summary: Orlah and kilayim of the vineyard join together, but Rabbi Shimon says they do not. Pieces of cloth, sack, leather and mat join together for tumah, because each could become tamei as a seat.

chunks.he: הָעָרְלָה וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם מִצְטָרְפִין זֶה עִם זֶה.
chunks.en: Orlah and kilayim of the vineyard join together.
chunks.st: The fruit of a tree during the first three years after its planting [orla] (see Leviticus 19:23), and diverse kinds,i.e., grain sown in a vineyard (see Deuteronomy 22:9) join together
chunks.stMore: to constitute the requisite measure to prohibit a mixture that they are mixed into. This applies when the volume of the permitted produce is less than two hundred times the prohibited produce.

words.note: Fruit of a tree in its first three years, which may not be eaten.
Grain planted in a vineyard, which is forbidden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: they do not join together.
chunks.st: They do not join together.
chunks.stMore: A garment must be at least three by three handbreadths in order to become a primary source of ritual impurity, by means of ritual impurity imparted by the treading of a zav. A sack made from goats’ hair must be at least four by four handbreadths, while an animal hide must be five by five, and a mat six by six.

chunks.en: Cloth and sack,
chunks.st: The garment and the sack,

chunks.en: sack and leather,
chunks.st: the sack and the hide,

chunks.en: leather and mat,
chunks.st: and the hide and the mat

chunks.en: join together.
chunks.st: all join together
chunks.stMore: to constitute the requisite measure to become ritually impure in accordance with the material of the greater measure.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says, why?
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said: What is the reason
chunks.stMore: that they join together, despite the fact that their requisite measures are not equal?

chunks.en: Because they all can become tamei as a seat.
chunks.explain: Each one could be used to patch a seat.
chunks.st: Because all the component materials are fit to become ritually impure through the ritual impurity imparted to a seat upon which a zav sits,
chunks.stMore: as they can each be used to patch a saddle or saddlecloth. Since the measure of all these materials is equal in the case of a zav, they join together for other forms of ritual impurity as well.
